text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London came under pressure following a weak performance in New York where funds and commission houses rolled nearby positions amid a perception of ample supply. At the close September stood $10 lower at $1,510 per tonne, while second-month November lost $8 to close at $1,529 per tonne.
Traders said absence of roaster demand weakened the support base, although some price fixing from trade bargain-hunters was seen on a scale basis to limit the slide.

Arabica futures in New York ended lower in the front months with even more pressure on the switches. Traders said ongoing, unsubstantiated talk that European trade houses may be shipping coffee to the United States for exchange certification has helped ease supply worries and dampened buyers' enthusiasm.

Additionally, industry sources expect the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report to show a modest build in US green coffee inventories during July. However, it is expected that lower quality coffee will account for the bulk of the expected increase. Data from Colombia today was negative given there was higher July production than previously anticipated.

Even after the recent slide in September the premium is still at 17.60 cents/lb. September lost 5.10 cents/lb to close at 183.10 cents/lb, while December shed 3.00 cents/lb to close at 165.50 cents/lb.

COLOMBIA - In coffee year 1996/97 (October/September) production up to July reached 9.3 million 60-kg bags, down from 11.4 million bags seen at the same stage last season. The Colombian Coffee Federation has forecast a total harvest of about 10 million bags for the 1996/97 cycle compared to 12.9 million bags produced the previous year.

The federation said Colombia's coffee exports, including federation and private exporters, totalled 804,000 bags in July compared to 894,000 bags in the same month last year. In calendar year 1997 up to July, Colombia has exported 6.5 million bags against 6 million bags in the same period in 1996.
In October/July 1996/97 Colombia has exported 9.6 million bags, slightly higher than the 9.4 million bags exported in the same period of 1995/96.

MEXICO - Mexico exported 130,080 bags of coffee in July 1997, sharply down from the 219,432 bags exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (October/July) up to 4.256 million bags which compares to 4.340 million bags exported the same period in 1995/96 and 2.971 million bags exported in 1994/95.
Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (October/September) reached 4.576 million bags, sharply up from the 3.258 million bags exported the previous year.

GERMANY - German net green coffee imports from outside the European Union totalled 1.173 million 60-kg bags in April 1997 after 1.081 million bags in March and 1.131 million bags in February, the DKV Coffee Association said. The total in calendar year 1996 was 11.98 million bags (11.65 million bags in 1995).

Colombia shipped 173,591 bags in April (15 per cent), Brazil 261,580 bags (22 per cent), Africa 204,624 bags (17 per cent), Central and South America 359,735 bags (31 per cent), Asia 172,594 bags (15 per cent) and others 353 (zero per cent).
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 606 bags as of August 12 to 92,959 bags. There were 5,853 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

NEW ZEALAND - New Zealand imported 79,600 bags of coffee in January/June 1997, 3 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 9 per cent to 162,900 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1997 were Indonesia (12,100 vs 15,600 bags), Vietnam (20,700 vs 15,800 bags) and Papua New Guinea (13,900 vs 13,200 bags).
